sm: The host traces how the Grand Theft Auto franchise grew despite decades of condemnation. It began in 1997 as a top-down game from a small Scottish studio, and Grand Theft Auto 3 in 2001 gave players an open city and sold about fourteen and a half million copies. San Andreas followed in 2004, and the 2005 Hot Coffee hidden minigame led to an adults-only rating, a recall costing an estimated twenty to twenty-five million dollars, and calls from Hillary Clinton for a federal investigation. The House voted 355 to 21 to ask the FTC to look into it. California's law banning violent game sales to minors was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2011, with Justice Scalia writing the majority opinion. Its author, state senator Leland Yee, was later arrested and sentenced to five years. Grand Theft Auto 4 and 5 broke launch records, and GTA 5 has sold more than two hundred thirty million copies, helped by GTA Online and its shark cards.

GTA 5 was re-released across three console generations, and the long wait for GTA 6 became an internet joke until a 2022 leak and the December 2023 reveal. The first trailer drew ninety million YouTube views in a day, and the second, in May 2025, drew about four hundred seventy-five million views across platforms. The game is set in Leonida, a fictional Florida, and is now due November 19th, 2026, after two delays. Cost estimates run from one billion to three billion dollars, and the host calculates that two billion dollars would need about thirty-six million copies to break even. Sensor Tower projects around twenty-five million pre-orders, and the host says a viral claim of thirty-nine million is unsupported. Other publishers avoided launching near it, and a Fort Stewart battalion offered a four-day pass to soldiers who re-enlisted. The game carries an M rating, and the host closes by calling it the biggest launch in entertainment history.
